judged_text: The computed schema keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] both evaluate to the literal key "[object Object]" (Zod schemas have no toString override), so minimumTokenResponseSchema enforces nothing beyond access_token and, because z.object strips unknown keys, silently drops every other field (expiry_date, instance_url, scope, refresh_token) from parsed token responses in credential-sharing mode. Self-hosters with credential sharing enabled get token payloads stripped to {access_token} persisted for Office365/Zoom/Salesforce, keeping the stale expired expiry_date and losing instance metadata, silently corrupting those integrations with a 200-looking success path.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` defines computed keys as `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. Those expressions are evaluated immediately as JS object-literal keys, producing a single literal property name (very likely `"[object Object]"`), and the second entry overwrites the first. As a result, the schema effectively validates only `{ access_token: string }` (plus an optional `"[object Object]"` field) and, because `z.object(...)` strips unknown keys by default, any real token fields like `expiry_date`, `expires_in`, `instance_url`, `scope`, etc. will be dropped in credential-sharing mode (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`). This parsed/stripped data is then used in multiple refresh flows (e.g., Office365 `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)`, Zoom `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseBody, zoomRefreshedTokenSchema)`, Salesforce `parseRefreshTokenResponse(accessTokenJson, salesforceTokenSchema)`), which can prevent updating expiry/metadata and can persist incomplete token payloads.
